history.dynasty: Later Gupta - inscription of King Adityasena (mid-to-late 7th century CE) recording a temple built on the hill
history.period: Early medieval (7th century CE inscription); Puranic/mythological references
history.summary: FLAG - CSV town and district wrong: Mandar Hill is at Bounsi, BANKA district (Bhagalpur division), about 45-50 km south of Bhagalpur city - not in Bhagalpur. It is a shared Jain-Hindu pilgrimage hill (~700 ft high, 12 temples): Jain tradition holds it as the site of three kalyanaks - diksha, kevala-jnana and nirvana - of the 12th Tirthankara Vasupujya; Hindu Puranas (Varaha, Garuda) and the Mahabharata associate it with the Samudra Manthan (churning of the ocean for amrit), with the serpent-rope coil marks said to be visible on the hill. The Paapharni pond beside the hill has a Vishnu-Lakshmi temple in its centre. Rare 11th-12th century sculptures of Shiva, Kamadhenu and Varaha lie scattered around the hill and await ASI conservation. The Mandar ropeway (377.36 m travel length) was inaugurated by Bihar's CM on 21 September 2021 (per GKToday). Coordinates from Wikipedia/GeoHack, corroborated by map sources.

name: Mandar Hill Temple (Mandar Parvat)
town_description: Bounsi (Bausi) is a small town in Banka district, Bihar, on the state highway between Bhagalpur and Dumka, known for Mandar Hill - the mythological Samudra Manthan site and a shared Jain-Hindu pilgrimage centre.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport (Jharkhand) is the nearest airport; Ranchi, Gaya, Patna and Kolkata airports are also listed (per Wikipedia).
travel.railway: Mandar Hill railway station on the Dumka-Bhagalpur line is the nearest (Howrah-Bhagalpur Vande Bharat and other expresses halt); Bhagalpur Junction is ~45 km away.
travel.road: On the state highway between Bhagalpur and Dumka; a ropeway (inaugurated September 2021) runs from the base to the hilltop.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; visit during the Makar Sankranti or Mahavir Jayanti fairs for the annual carnival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Ropeway reportedly 9:00 AM-1:00 PM and 2:00-5:00 PM, closed Wednesdays (per a Justdial listing - verify); temples generally open during daytime
